source.publication: 2025 Complete Income Tax Instruction Booklet (ip25), Kansas Department of Revenue, with Form K-40 and Schedule S bound in (PDF pages 19-22)
source.section: Form K-40 lines 1-12 (ip25 PDF page 20; exemption block PDF page 19); K-40 instructions lines 1-3 (PDF page 6), line 4 and exemptions (PDF page 6), lines 5-8 (PDF page 7); Schedule S line A10 (ip25 PDF page 21), instructions PDF page 11; FAQ 'Are Social Security benefits taxable to Kansas?' (https://www.ksrevenue.gov/faqs-taxii.html); WORKSHEET - Standard Deduction for People 65 or Older and/or Blind (PDF page 6); tax rate schedule: 2025 Tax Computation Worksheet (PDF page 34) and Tax Table (PDF pages 27-34)

worked: Federal AGI = IRA distribution (you) 50,000.00 + taxable Social Security 25,500.00 = 75,500.00. Federal taxable income = 75,500.00 - standard deduction 17,750.00 (15,750.00 + 1 x 2,000.00 for 65 or older) = 57,750.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; federal figures are given, not tested; Kansas starts from federal AGI). Schedule S Part A: line A1 0.00; lines A2-A8 0.00; line A9 total additions 0.00. Line A10 Social Security benefits included in federal AGI 25,500.00 (no income test for 2025); lines A11-A13 0.00; line A14 0.00; lines A15-A25 0.00; line A26 total subtractions = 25,500.00; line A27 net modification = 0.00 - 25,500.00 = -25,500.00. Form K-40: line 1 federal AGI 75,500.00; line 2 modifications -25,500.00; line 3 Kansas AGI = 75,500.00 + (-25,500.00) = 50,000.00; line 4 standard deduction (single), worksheet for people 65 or older: 1 box checked, 3,605.00 + 1 x 850.00 = 4,455.00 (the worksheet prints 4,455.00); line 5 exemption allowance (1 exemption) 9,160.00, 0 dependents; line 6 total deductions = 4,455.00 + 9,160.00 = 13,615.00; line 7 taxable income = 50,000.00 - 13,615.00 = 36,385.00; line 8 tax (rate schedule as numbers, PDF page 34): 5.2% x 23,000.00 = 1,196.00 + 5.58% x (36,385.00 - 23,000.00 = 13,385.00) = 746.8830; total 1,942.8830 = 1,942.88. Line 7 is 100,000 or less, so the form reads the tax table: row 36,351-36,400, single, head of household or married filing separate column, PDF page 29, gives 1,942; expected keeps the formula figure. Lines 9-10 do not apply (resident); line 11 0.00; line 12 total income tax 1,942.88. Credits (lines 13-15, 17): none, 0.00; state income tax = 1,942.88. Federal AGI holds 85% of the 30,000.00 benefit. Line A10 takes out what federal AGI holds, so nothing of the benefit is left in Kansas income.
accepted_approximations: A pension from another state's government, private pensions, IRA and other employer-plan distributions and Roth conversions stay in Kansas income: no line subtracts them. This is read from the booklet's silence, not from a sentence saying they are taxed.
Tax is computed from the rates, not the printed tables and rounded worksheet subtraction.
